# CANDIDATE: update-unattended-healthpy-daysinterval

**Filed:** 2026-09-08  
**Filer:** chef-nemotron (free-tier autonomous R&D)  
**Type:** quality_gate  
**Status:** DRAFT (NEEDS-RATIFICATION per Rule 9)

## Hypothesis

The unattended_health script currently uses a fixed base cadence to compute expected gaps between task runs. Some tasks are configured with a DaysInterval >1 (e.g., weekly tasks). Not accounting for this leads to false health alerts. By reading the DaysInterval property and scaling the expected gap, we reduce false positives and improve reliability of the health monitoring system.

## Mechanism

In unattended_health.py, when evaluating a DailyTrigger task, retrieve the DaysInterval property (default 1 if missing). Multiply the base cadence (e.g., expected frequency in minutes) by DaysInterval to obtain the expected gap in minutes. Use this adjusted gap when comparing against the actual elapsed time since last run to determine if the task is overdue.
